title: Cap. VIII Resp. Primo: slippery consequence — cause of the permitted thing is not cause of the permission
pass_a_gloss: First, what is argued, The sins of the reprobate are the cause of all the effects of reprobation: Therefore also of the thing itself, namely of Divine reprobation, as it regards those effects, this consequence is altogether slippery and weak, if all those evils be called effects which follow it. For that can be the cause of the permitted thing which is not the cause of the permission related to the permitted thing. For example, I see two drunken men rashly wandering hither and thither; I foresee that both will fall into a pit, and there perish by hunger, unless provision be made for them thence. I decree in my mind to warn one of them, to draw him back, and efficaciously to free him from this peril; the other not to warn, not to draw back; or at least not so to warn and draw back that in fact he be freed. Now that latter has fallen into the pit, there he lies long, is wasted, and at length is extinguished by hunger.
pass_b_english: First: the argument — sins of the reprobate cause all reprobation's effects; therefore also divine reprobation itself as regards those effects — is a slippery, weak consequence if every evil that follows is called an effect. What causes the permitted thing need not cause the permission of that thing. Example: I see two drunken men wandering rashly about; I foresee both will fall into a pit and starve there unless helped. I resolve to warn one, draw him back, and free him from the peril; the other I will not warn or draw back — or at least not so as actually to free him. That latter falls into the pit, lies long, wastes, and at last starves.
source_text: Primo, quod arguitur, Peccata reprobi sunt causa omnium effectorum reprobationis: Ergo etiam et ipsius rei, scilicet reprobationis Divinae, ut respicit illos effectus, haec prorsus consequentia lubrica est et infirma, si ea omnia mala vocentur effecta quae eam consequuntur. Nam illud potest esse causa rei permissae quod non sit causa permissionis relatae ad rem permissam. Verbi gratia, video duos ebrios homines temere hac illuc errantes; praevideo utrumque in foveam lapsurum, et fame ibi periturum, nisi inde illis prospiciatur. Decerno apud animum alterum eorum monere, retrahere, et ab hoc periculo efficaciter liberare; alterum non monere, non retrahere; aut saltem non ita monere et retrahere ut de facto liberetur. Decidit jam iste posterior in foveam, ibi diu jacet, maceratur, et tandem fame exstinguitur.
